stories.headline: Iran missile hits US Embassy in Baghdad, drone debris ignites fire at UAE Fujairah oil terminal

key_facts.fact: A missile struck a helipad inside the US Embassy compound in Baghdad on Saturday, the second attack on the embassy since the US-Israel war on Iran began on February 28.
key_facts.excerpt: A missile struck a helipad inside the U.S. Embassy compound in Baghdad ... as the U.S.-Israel war with Iran entered its third week Saturday.

key_facts.fact: Debris from an intercepted Iranian drone struck an oil facility in Fujairah, UAE, triggering a major fire at the strategic oil terminal; some oil loading operations at the port were suspended.
key_facts.excerpt: A fire broke out at oil storage facilities in Fujairah following the drone strike. The port, one of the world's largest oil storage and bunkering hubs, was reportedly hit by multiple drones.

key_facts.fact: In Dubai, debris from a missile intercepted by UAE air defence systems hit the facade of a building in central Dubai, marking the second such incident in as many days.
key_facts.excerpt: In Dubai, debris from a missile intercepted by the UAE's air defence systems hit the façade of a building in central Dubai on Saturday, marking the second such incident in as many days.

key_facts.fact: The US has struck over 15,000 enemy targets since the war began, averaging more than 1,000 daily, while Iran continued widespread missile and drone attacks on Israel and Gulf Arab states.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran has continued to launch widespread missile and drone attacks on Israel and Gulf Arab states.

stories.headline: Iran warns UAE to evacuate Jebel Ali, Khalifa, and Fujairah ports, threatens regional oil infrastructure

key_facts.fact: Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya military command warned UAE residents to evacuate areas near Jebel Ali port in Dubai, Khalifa port in Abu Dhabi, and Fujairah port, calling them 'legitimate targets'.
key_facts.excerpt: Tehran has claimed that the US used ports and jetties in the UAE to attack Iran's Abu Mousa Island, making them 'legitimate' targets for retaliation and urged civilians to evacuate.

key_facts.fact: Iran's armed forces said any attack on Iran's oil and energy infrastructure will lead to attacks on energy infrastructure owned by oil companies cooperating with the US in the region.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's armed forces said Saturday that any attack on Iran's oil and energy infrastructure will lead to attacks on energy infrastructure owned by oil companies cooperating with the U.S. in the region.

key_facts.fact: Iran FM Abbas Araghchi called on Gulf nations to expel US forces, saying the American security umbrella is 'full of holes'.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran FM Calls on Gulf Nations to Expel US Forces, Says American Security Umbrella 'Full of Holes'; IRGC Warns UAE Ports Jebel Ali Khalifa Next Legitimate Targets

key_facts.fact: Iran claimed the US used 'ports, docks and hideouts' in the UAE to launch strikes on Iran's Kharg Island, without providing evidence.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran threatened to attack cities in the UAE, home to Dubai and one of the world's busiest airports, saying the U.S. used 'ports, docks and hideouts' there to launch strikes on Iran's Kharg Island, without providing evidence.

stories.headline: Trump rejects Iran ceasefire offer, demands Tehran abandon nuclear ambitions before any deal

key_facts.fact: Trump told NBC that Iran 'wants to make a deal' but he rejected it because 'the terms aren't good enough yet', saying any agreement must be 'very solid' and include Tehran abandoning nuclear ambitions.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Iran wants to make a deal, and I don't want to make it because the terms aren't good enough yet,' he said, adding that any terms would need to be 'very solid' for the US to engage in negotiations.

key_facts.fact: Iran rejected the possibility of any ceasefire until US and Israeli strikes end; several countries including Oman and Egypt have been trying to mediate without success.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran, for its part, has rejected the possibility of any ceasefire until US and Israeli strikes end, two senior Iranian sources told Reuters, adding that several countries had been trying to mediate an end to the conflict.

key_facts.fact: The war has killed more than 2,000 people as both sides dig in for an extended conflict, with Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz sending oil prices soaring.
key_facts.excerpt: The lack of interest from Washington and Tehran suggests both sides are digging in for an extended conflict, even as the widening war inflicts civilian casualties... The war has killed more than 2,000 peop[le].

key_facts.fact: Iranian FM Araghchi said the Islamic Republic is open to 'any regional initiative that leads to a fair end to the war', but added that no specific proposal has yet been presented.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the Islamic Republic is open to 'any regional initiative that leads to a fair end to the war,' according to an interview published by the UK-based Al-Araby Al-Jadeed.

key_facts.fact: Trump called on China, France, Japan, South Korea and the UK to send warships to keep the Strait of Hormuz open, describing it as a 'team effort'.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump mentioned China – the top purchaser of Iranian oil – as well as leading economies France, Japan, South Korea, and the United Kingdom.

stories.headline: US deploys 5,000 Marines to Middle East; France rejects Trump's Strait of Hormuz warship call

key_facts.fact: Approximately 5,000 additional Marines and sailors are deploying to the Middle East to support the war in Iran, including the 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit from the Indo-Pacific.
key_facts.excerpt: The deployment of about 2,500 Marines to the Middle East represents a new phase in the two-week-old war in Iran, as Iranian forces increase their attacks on the Strait of Hormuz.

key_facts.fact: The 31st MEU will enable the Pentagon to launch raids onto islands near the Strait of Hormuz to counter Iranian fast boats carrying mines, raising the risk of ground escalation.
key_facts.excerpt: With the arrival of the 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit... the Pentagon will be able to quickly launch raids onto the islands with infantry Marines who will have logistics and air support.

key_facts.fact: France rejected Trump's call to send warships to the Strait of Hormuz; the French MFA said 'France's mission remains defensive and protective. Stop the scaremongering.'
key_facts.excerpt: The official X account for the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs refuted these claims. 'No,' the post reads... 'Aircraft carrier and its group staying the eastern Mediterranean. Posture has not changed: defensive it is.'

key_facts.fact: France's Defence Minister Catherine Vautrin had already stated Paris has no plans to send naval vessels to the Strait of Hormuz and that France is not participating in the war.
key_facts.excerpt: France on Sunday denied reports that it had dispatched warships to the Strait of Hormuz following a request from US President Donald Trump... the French carrier strike group remains stationed in the eastern Mediterranean.

stories.headline: Meta planning sweeping layoffs of up to 20% of workforce (~16,000 jobs) to fund AI infrastructure

key_facts.fact: Meta is preparing to lay off approximately 20% of its workforce, roughly 16,000 workers out of about 79,000 employees, to fund AI infrastructure buildout costing $64-72 billion in 2026 alone.
key_facts.excerpt: Reuters reported that Meta was gearing up to cut approximately 20 percent of its workforce, which would account for roughly 16,000 workers.

key_facts.fact: Two senior employees said the layoffs could begin within a month; senior leaders have been asked to model leaner teams across the company.
key_facts.excerpt: People familiar with the plan told Reuters the timeline and final numbers are still under discussion, but senior leaders have been asked to model leaner teams across the company.

key_facts.fact: If confirmed, the layoffs would be Meta's largest since 2022 when it eliminated 11,000 jobs during the 'year of efficiency' restructuring, followed by 10,000 more in 2023.
key_facts.excerpt: If true, the layoffs would be the most significant cut to its staff since 2022, when it eliminated 11,000 jobs. The following year, the company laid off another 10,000.

key_facts.fact: Meta has said it plans to pour approximately $600 billion into AI infrastructure and data centers by 2028, and has spent hundreds of millions to attract AI researchers to its superintelligence team.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta has previously said it plans to pour approximately $600 billion into new AI infrastructure and data centers by 2028, a necessary investment for its AI ambitions.

key_facts.fact: Meta spokesperson Andy Stone called the Reuters report 'speculative', which analysts noted in corporate language often means the numbers are real but the timing is not yet finalized.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's spokesperson called the report 'speculative,' which in corporate parlance often means the number is real but the announcement timing is not yet finalized.

stories.headline: Oil prices whipsaw as Kharg Island strikes and expanding Gulf war rattle global energy markets

key_facts.fact: WTI crude surged to an intraday high of $119.43 during the week — the largest weekly gain in WTI history — before correcting to the $87-89 range, then spiking again after the Kharg Island bombing.
key_facts.excerpt: WTI closed the prior week near $88 and screamed to an intraday high of $119.43 on Monday... a 35.6% surge that marked the largest weekly gain in WTI history.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude surged 9% to $101.13 after the US struck military targets on Kharg Island, which handles 90% of Iran's oil exports.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. military strikes on Iran's Kharg Island triggered a 9% surge in Brent crude to $101.13, marking a 28% post-attack price spike.

key_facts.fact: Hundreds of tankers sit idle on both sides of the Strait of Hormuz as Iran has effectively closed the waterway, pushing oil above $100 — the highest since 2022.
key_facts.excerpt: Hundreds of tankers sit idle on both sides of the Strait of Hormuz as Iran has effectively closed the waterway, pushing oil prices above $100 – the highest since 2022.

key_facts.fact: Taking out Kharg infrastructure would remove 2 million barrels per day from the market permanently, according to Pickering Energy Partners' chief investment officer.
key_facts.excerpt: 'You take out Kharg infrastructure, then you take 2 million bpd out of the market for good – not until the Straits get fixed,' said Dan Pickering, chief investment officer for Pickering Energy Partners.

key_facts.fact: IEA and oil-producing nations are discussing a coordinated strategic petroleum reserve release to calm markets, though analysts say it cannot fix the underlying Hormuz disruption.
key_facts.excerpt: Record oil release steadies markets, but war-driven disruption in the Strait of Hormuz will keep global energy supplies uncertain.

stories.headline: US job openings rise to 7 million in January, beating expectations despite sluggish hiring

key_facts.fact: US job openings rose to 6.95 million in January, up from 6.55 million in December, beating economist forecasts in a JOLTS report released on Friday.
key_facts.excerpt: The 6.95 million job postings in January were up from 6.55 million in December, the Labor Department said Friday. That was higher than economists had forecast.

key_facts.fact: Initial jobless claims fell to 213,000 for the week ending March 7, near historic lows and below the pre-pandemic average of 220,000.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. initial jobless claims fell to 213,000 for the week ending March 7, staying near historic lows and well below the pre-pandemic average of 220,000.

key_facts.fact: Despite low layoffs, the US economy shed 92,000 jobs last month and in 2025 added fewer than 10,000 jobs per month — the weakest hiring outside recession years since 2002.
key_facts.excerpt: Last month, employers cut 92,000 jobs. In 2025, they added fewer than 10,000 jobs a month, weakest hiring outside recession years since 2002.

key_facts.fact: Job openings remain far below their peak of 12.3 million in March 2022, with hiring momentum slowing as time-to-hire stretches to 44 days.
key_facts.excerpt: Hiring momentum has slowed significantly, with job openings down to 7.6 million from a peak of 12.2 million and time-to-hire stretching to 44 days.

stories.headline: Vimgreen's A2AR antagonist receives world's first NASH/MASH clinical trial clearance in China

key_facts.fact: Vimgreen Pharmaceuticals received CDE (China's Center for Drug Evaluation) IND approval for VG081821 in NASH/MASH, the first global clearance of an A2A receptor antagonist for NASH clinical investigation.
key_facts.excerpt: This approval constitutes the first global clearance of an A2A receptor antagonist for NASH clinical investigation.

key_facts.fact: VG081821 can proceed directly to Phase II NASH trials, significantly shortening the clinical development timeline for this potential breakthrough therapy.
key_facts.excerpt: VG081821 can proceed directly to Phase II NASH trials, significantly shortening the clinical development timeline for this potential breakthrough.

key_facts.fact: This is the second clinical indication for Vimgreen's lead drug candidate, complementing its ongoing development program for Parkinson's disease.
key_facts.excerpt: This achievement represents the second clinical indication for the company's lead drug candidate, complementing its ongoing development program for Parkinson's disease.

sources.title: Vimgreen's Novel A2AR Antagonist Receives CDE IND Approval for NASH/MASH Therapy
